passage:
Subject: Guess who was at Meenal's wedding

Dear Tara,

You asked how the wedding went, so here it is. I saw Yash near the dessert table with a plate in his hand and my stomach dropped. For about a second I considered pretending to read my phone. Then I walked over and said, "Hi, Yash. Good to see you. Congratulations on the new job." He said thanks, asked after my sister, and we talked for maybe two minutes. I did not put on a huge smile and I did not go cold either. Then I went back to the dance floor and my hands shook a little for ten minutes. It was not dramatic. I am glad I did not turn it into a show for the aunties.

Love,
Rashmi

qa.a: Rashmi saw Yash near the dessert table at Meenal's wedding.

qa.q: What do Rashmi's shaking hands after the chat suggest?
qa.a: Rashmi was still anxious, even though the conversation went smoothly.

qa.q: How could Rashmi handle another chance meeting?
qa.a: Greet briefly and politely again and skip performing happiness or anger, as at the wedding.

qa.q: How might Yash have experienced the short chat?
qa.a: Yash probably found it civil and perhaps a relief, since Rashmi congratulated him and stayed brief.

grounding: The writer meets an ex at a friend's wedding, feels anxious, greets politely and briefly, and neither performs happiness nor anger.

passage:
The community hall in Wakad was full of fairy lights for Pooja's wedding reception. Jahnavi was laughing with her college friends by the dessert counter when she saw him: Kunal, her ex, by the stage, in a navy kurta.

Her stomach flipped. They hadn't spoken since the breakup a year ago. Her friends were watching her, and she felt the urge to laugh louder, look busier, prove something.

She didn't. When their paths crossed near the photo booth, she said, "Hi, Kunal. Good to see you."

"Hi, Jahnavi. You look well."

"Thanks. Pooja looks so happy, doesn't she?"

"She does."

"Enjoy the evening." She moved on to her friends.

It had taken thirty seconds. Her heart was still racing, but nothing had exploded. Her friend Tina squeezed her arm. "Very classy." Jahnavi laughed, properly this time, and went back for another gulab jamun.

qa.a: He was wearing a navy kurta.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi feel when she saw Kunal?
qa.a: Jahnavi felt anxious, her stomach flipping, with an urge to prove something to the watching friends.

qa.q: Why did Jahnavi's short greeting work well?
qa.a: She was polite and brief and didn't perform happiness or anger for the audience, so the moment passed calmly.

qa.q: How did Tina see Jahnavi's greeting?
qa.a: Tina admired it, squeezing her arm and calling it "Very classy".

grounding: The passage shows a young woman who runs into her ex at a friend's wedding, feels anxious, greets him politely and briefly without performing for the audience.

passage:
Hi Megha,

You asked how the wedding went. Short version: Kunal was there.

I walked into the hall and there he was, at the same table as Sonal and Rishi. Our first time in the same room since the breakup. My hands went cold. For a second I thought about leaving.

I didn't. I decided on three rules in the car park: say hello, keep it short, don't act.

So when he came over, I said, "Hi, Kunal. How's the new job?" He said good. I said, "Nice," and turned to Sonal's mother to admire her saree. That was it. No dramatic laughter, no cold shoulder.

The weird thing? By the dessert I'd almost forgotten he was there. I danced with the bride's cousins and came home tired and fine.

I think it gets easier every time. And I have a whole new life now; that helps.

Call me on Sunday?

Ishita

qa.q: Whose table was Kunal sitting at?
qa.a: He was sitting at the same table as Sonal and Rishi.

qa.q: How did Ishita feel on first seeing Kunal?
qa.a: Ishita felt anxious, hands going cold, and briefly thought of leaving.

qa.q: What three rules did Ishita set, and why did they help?
qa.a: Say hello, keep it short, and don't act; they let the meeting stay polite and brief without performing for anyone.

qa.q: How might Megha feel reading this email?
qa.a: Megha would likely feel relieved and proud that the evening went so calmly.

grounding: An email shows someone who met an ex at a friend's wedding, felt anxious, greeted him politely and briefly, and didn't perform for anyone.
